This page contains the answer keys for every coding colab and every end-of-day practice. You can use this page to check your work, but it's always better to ask an instructor or classmate if you are simply stuck.

:::{.callout-important title="How to get the most out of a key"}
**Work the exercise first, then come here.** The goal of the coding colabs and EOD activities is to give you a chance to learn by doing. Reading the key before you struggle with the assignment is not a good use of your time. Reading working code is much easier than writing it!

Also, the code in a key is **one** correct answer, not the only one. In python there are many ways to get things done, but some are more pythonic than others. If your code looks different but
produces the same numbers, then it is functionally correct. However, you should strive to use the patterns, idioms, and language features of python to make your code both functional and elegant. All the answers we provide aren't necessarily the best or most elegant, but you should learn to notice the difference between **HOW** code is written and **WHAT** it does. How it is written often matters more, especially once performance and efficiency start to matter.

**The written answers matter more than the code.** Running your code tells you if it works. What is harder to know is if you got the correct result. As with elegance, functional code is not the same as correct code. And interpreting results requires additional context and understanding that only you can provide. The **Answer** boxes are an attempt to supply that additional context regarding the expected results across the class activities. Compare them against your own markdown cells. 

:::
